state.question: Why do the four measurement streams show near-zero or negative cross-correlations at various time offsets, with only pendulum_obs showing a moderately strong autocorrelation at 7-day lag (0.600), while all other instruments show weak or negative autocorrelations—suggesting either systematic measurement incompatibility, environmental coupling we haven't identified, or instrumental drift that hasn't yet declared itself as a level shift?

hypotheses.label: Four independent instruments with good baselines; apparent weak correlations are statistical noise from small sample sizes and multiple offset trials (look-elsewhere effect).
hypotheses.rationale: This is the null hypothesis and must carry substantial weight. With n=24–60 per cross-check and ~10 offsets searched per pair, the chance thresholds I computed (±0.374 to ±0.592) properly account for multiple comparisons. Most observed correlations fall *within* or only marginally exceed these thresholds. The strongest signal is pendulum_obs autocorrelation at lag 7 (0.600 vs. threshold ±0.684), which is *not* significant by my own chance expectation. No level shifts detected. The instruments have tight value spacing (min 0.0001) and appropriate trial counts for 10-day baselines. I should expect weak correlations between physically independent systems. Pending post-baseline drift analysis will test stability.

hypotheses.label: Systematic environmental coupling (thermal, vibration, or electromagnetic) is correlated across some instrument pairs but not others, creating spurious negative correlations and the pendulum_obs 7-day cycle.
hypotheses.rationale: The resonator_lab ↔ resonator_obs pair shows the strongest signal: -0.677 at 5-day offset, exceeding chance threshold (±0.529) by ~28%. Both are resonator-type instruments in different locations (lab vs. obs). If a shared environmental driver (e.g., weekly settlement activity, thermal cycling) couples differently to lab and observatory resonators due to geometry or shielding, we'd expect anti-correlation and time-lag structure. The pendulum_obs 7-day autocorrelation (0.600) is suggestive of a cyclic environmental influence (work week? thermal pattern?). However: (i) pendulum_lab shows no equivalent cycle, (ii) no mechanism yet identified, (iii) only one pair clearly exceeds chance. This remains speculative without environmental monitoring data.

hypotheses.label: Instrumental drift is present but subtle: baseline period too short (10 days) to distinguish real drift from noise; post-baseline measurements will reveal systematic changes in mean or variance.
hypotheses.rationale: Baselines of n=90, 114, 66, 60 over 10 days should detect large drift (e.g., >1% per day), but small systematic trends (~0.1–0.3% per day) are difficult to resolve. The weak autocorrelations at non-zero lags (especially negative values in resonators) *could* reflect unresolved instrument aging or gain/offset creep. The exact repetition counts (max 1 reading) are as expected and don't rule out drift.
